name: Frosted tips

card.summary: A hairstyle with bleached or lightened tips over darker roots, adding contrast and texture to short hair.
card.note: Bleaching can dry and damage hair.

quick.overview:
Frosted tips is a men's hair style in which the ends of the hair are lightened to blonde or platinum against darker roots. It adds visual contrast and highlights texture and spikes.

It peaked in the late 1990s and early 2000s with boy bands and returned in subtler versions in the 2010s and 2020s.
quick.how: Salons lighten only the tips, then tone them; wearers use purple shampoo and conditioner and re-lighten as hair grows, with styling gel or texturizer for spikes or a tousled finish.
quick.risks: Bleach can dry or weaken hair, and grown-out roots need upkeep; professional application is commonly advised.

lead: Frosted tips is a hairstyle, mainly worn by men, where the hair ends are bleached or highlighted lighter against darker roots. This contrast emphasizes the texture and volume of short to medium hair.[1]
It rose in the late 1990s through boy bands such as NSYNC and faded by the mid-2000s, with revivals around 2017 and 2025.[1]

angle.text: Wearers lighten just the ends to add dimension and a bolder style without coloring the whole head.

infobox: Purple shampoo, re-lightening every few weeks

paras: The style is credited to late-1990s pop culture and boy bands, with Justin Timberlake the best-known example, and it returned in 2017 with figures such as Chris Evans and in 2025 with Robert Pattinson.[1]
Reported upkeep includes toning shampoo and conditioning of bleached ends.[1]
